2027-11-09.title: The Mission of the Church
2027-11-09.verse: He told them, “You are not permitted to know the times or periods that the Father has set by his own authority. But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the farthest parts of the earth.
2027-11-09.observation: Have you ever wondered what the mission of the church is? The mission of the church is to make disciples of everyone, all over the world. We are not like Islam, which also believes it is supposed to do this but does it with domination and destruction. God tells His Church to do so with love and compassion. The purpose of the Church is to be an outpost of Heaven on Earth. We are to show His goodness and show the world that the love of God that changed our lives will change theirs as well.
2027-11-09.application: Take the goodness of God with you into your world today. Share it with someone.
2027-11-09.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for giving us the opportunity to share Your love with someone today.

2027-11-10.title: The Secret Sauce of the Early Church
2027-11-10.verse: They were devoting themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. Reverential awe came over everyone, and many wonders and miraculous signs came about by the apostles. All who believed were together and held everything in common, and they began selling their property and possessions and distributing the proceeds to everyone, as anyone had need. Every day they continued to gather together by common consent in the temple courts, breaking bread from house to house, sharing their food with glad and humble hearts, praising God and having the good will of all the people. And the Lord was adding to their number every day those who were being saved.
2027-11-10.observation: When the Holy Spirit descended upon the Church, the result was many people becoming new Christ followers. As a leader, my immediate thought is wondering about their next step. What did they do to make the most of this opportunity? How did they organize themselves and move forward? What was the secret sauce? We know from a little later, they did organize themselves and develop leaders. Organization is a good thing. However, in this situation, they did not try to over-systemize what God had done. They loved each other. They kept themselves unified. They did life together. The secret sauce of the early church was to love each other and share that love with others. This is a great lesson for us today.
2027-11-10.application: Show love in everything you do today.
2027-11-10.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for loving us and showing us how to love others.

2027-11-11.title: Give What You Have Received
2027-11-11.verse: But Peter said, “I have no silver or gold, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, stand up and walk!
2027-11-11.observation: I have talked to many Christians who are intimidated by the world around them. They see people hurting and feel so inadequate to help. They also realize they do not have life figured out yet either and end up feeling as though they are not up to the task of being God’s “hands and feet” in their world. Today’s passage reminds us that we are not supposed to be everyone’s savior. We are supposed to point them to the One who is. Peter and John could have said they were not up to the task because they were not Jesus. Instead, they said they could give only what they have received and that was enough. Today, do not see your world as something you have to save. Instead, see the world as a place where you can point people to Jesus. He is the Savior. We are the messengers.
2027-11-11.application: Today, share with someone the hope you have received.
2027-11-11.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being the true Savior of the world.

2027-11-12.title: Be A Giver
2027-11-12.verse: When they had prayed, the place where they were assembled together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak the word of God courageously. The group of those who believed were of one heart and mind, and no one said that any of his possessions was his own, but everything was held in common. With great power the apostles were giving testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was on them all. For there was no one needy among them because those who were owners of land or houses were selling them and bringing the proceeds from the sales and placing them at the apostles’ feet. The proceeds were distributed to each, as anyone had need.
2027-11-12.observation: The power of God leads us to be a giver to those around us. I have been around Christians who think the purpose of experiencing the power of God is to have an emotional high. They treat the presence of God like a drug and they are the heroin addict. Every Sunday is their chance to get a fresh high. However, this passage shows us that the power of God empowers us to go be a difference maker and do things we could not do alone. There is nothing wrong with experiencing the presence of God. The time to course correct is when we see God’s presence as the point rather than the fuel. The presence of God in our lives is the fuel that empowers us to be His Hands and Feet in the world.
2027-11-12.application: Today, allow the Lord to empower you to be a difference maker in someone’s life.
2027-11-12.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being the Source of our hope.

2027-11-13.title: Let Them See Over Time
2027-11-13.verse: So in this case I say to you, stay away from these men and leave them alone because if this plan or this undertaking originates with people, it will come to nothing, but if it is from God, you will not be able to stop them, or you may even be found fighting against God.” He convinced them,
2027-11-13.observation: The bottom line of the argument in this passage is wait and see what they will do when the “new” wears off. Anyone can get excited about something new and fresh. What you do after something is no longer new says more about the difference it made in your life. As a pastor, I have learned to use the “newness” of salvation as a way to motivate people to develop healthy spiritual habits. This is because I know the “new” will wear off and it will be time to grow. It is then that people will begin to realize that the goodness of God does not fade over time. The book of Lamentations says the mercies of the Lord are new every morning and His faithfulness is great. We can experience the freshness of the Lord every day. This will truly show people how good the Lord is.
2027-11-13.application: Don’t live on emotion. Live on relationship.
2027-11-13.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being worth following over the course of our lives.

2027-11-14.title: We All Can Make A Difference
2027-11-14.verse: So the twelve called the whole group of the disciples together and said, “It is not right for us to neglect the word of God to wait on tables. But carefully select from among you, brothers, seven men who are well-attested, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may put in charge of this necessary task. But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.” The proposal pleased the entire group, so they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, with Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas, a Gentile convert to Judaism from Antioch.
2027-11-14.observation: The early days of the church seem full of motion and activity. As the church was growing, they were working out how to properly care for one another. The model of the synagogues of the time meant they had the duty to help one another in times of need. This is a great thing, but it can be overwhelming when the need is overwhelming. Instead of trying to do it all, the disciples realized their limitations. They also realized what was most important for them to do. They recognized they were not the only ones gifted. Everyone had the capacity to make a difference. This reality is still true today. We all have the ability to make a difference. Just like the disciples, we need to figure out what we can do and do it with all our might. Then, make room for someone else so they can make a difference, too. Then, we work together for the good of others and the glory of God.
2027-11-14.application: How can you make a difference today?
2027-11-14.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for empowering us all to make a difference in our world.

2027-11-16.title: A Vision for What Matters Most
2027-11-16.verse: But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently toward heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God. “Look!” he said. “I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!
2027-11-16.observation: I can imagine that Stephen did not want the title of being the first Christian martyr. What would cause Stephen to stand against such overwhelming opposition? How could he be so bold when it seemed as though he stood alone? The answer is he was not standing alone. The Bible gives us a look into what Stephen saw. He did not see himself standing alone against the enemies of God. He was standing with Jesus, who stood at the right hand of God. He had a clear picture of who he was fighting for and why it all mattered. When facing the difficulties of life, we must always be careful to have a clear picture of what matters most. Then, we will never feel alone and no holy cause ever feels hopeless.
2027-11-16.application: Get a clear picture of Jesus and move forward for Him today.
2027-11-16.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being worth standing for in a world that doesn’t yet see You.

2027-11-17.title: God Orders Our Steps
2027-11-17.verse: Then an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south on the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.” (This is a desert road.) So he got up and went. There he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was in charge of all her treasury. He had come to Jerusalem to worship,
2027-11-17.observation: The Holy Spirit placed Philip at the right place. Philip knew how the book of Isaiah spoke of Jesus and was ready to answer the eunuch’s questions. The eunuch was moved by the Holy Spirit to read the scroll of Isaiah that day and was ready to think over what it meant. When you think about it, there were many different circumstances that had to come together for this moment to happen. Philip needed to be passing that way and close enough to hear the eunuch reading. The eunuch needed to be in a place where he was willing to listen. There are so many details that came together and God was orchestrating them all. If we truly believe God is sovereign and we are truly living as close to Him as we can, we can expect Him to put us in the right moment to make a difference for Him. Our job is to pay attention and take the next step.
2027-11-17.application: Keep your eyes open for God’s “coincidences” today.
2027-11-17.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for giving us the honor of serving You.

2027-11-18.title: God Knows How To Get Our Attention
2027-11-18.verse: As he was going along, approaching Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him. He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?
2027-11-18.observation: I often hear people worried about missing what God is trying to do in their lives. It’s a beautiful thing to want to know what God is up to so we can stay in step with His plan. However, we need to challenge this thought process a little. This would indicate that God is timid, shy, and uncertain about how to get our attention. This is almost as if God is waiting on us and is so subtle that we will miss Him. The King of the universe is not timid, shy, or unable to steer our lives. A better way to think about this is to realize that God often moves in “nudges” and not big moments like the passage explains in today’s text. However, it is also important to realize that God can and does know how to get our attention. Therefore, we keep our eyes open and trust that when we need to turn, He will turn us. Never doubt God’s love for you or His ability to get our attention. Instead, we must always realize that God is getting our attention and not destroying us. Paul could have seen this moment as God’s judgment. Rather, he saw it for what it was. God was changing his direction. Could it be possible that the difficult thing you are going through is not God punishing you but God changing your direction or getting your attention? If this is true, we should stop asking why and start asking, “What do You want me to see?”
2027-11-18.application: Reframe your current difficulties as God steering you, not destroying you.
2027-11-18.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for always looking out for our ultimate best.

2027-11-19.title: Add God to Your Schedule
2027-11-19.verse: Now there was a man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of what was known as the Italian Cohort. He was a devout, God-fearing man, as was all his household; he did many acts of charity for the people and prayed to God regularly. About three o’clock one afternoon he saw clearly in a vision an angel of God who came in and said to him, “Cornelius.
2027-11-19.observation: Though Cornelius was a Roman officer, he followed the Jewish customs. This meant he was to pray three times a day. One of the times was 3pm or the 9th hour of the day. It was during his scheduled time of worship that the Lord spoke to him and changed his life. I have had many times when people told me they needed to hear from God. However, they expected God to interrupt their schedule and speak to them. God can do this. However, most of the time God will speak to you when He is part of your life, not an interruption. You might be surprised how often you can have an encounter with God when you add Him to your daily schedule.
2027-11-19.application: Make an appointment with God every day and don’t miss it. If you do, don’t miss two.
2027-11-19.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for wanting to meet with us every day.

2027-11-20.title: Be a Finder
2027-11-20.verse: Then Barnabas departed for Tarsus to look for Saul, and when he found him, he brought him to Antioch. So for a whole year Barnabas and Saul met with the church and taught a significant number of people. Now it was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.
2027-11-20.observation: Saul was minding his business in obscurity, when Barnabas went to find him. Too many people want to identify themselves with Saul, but I think you should think more like Barnabas. Too many people see themselves as someone needing to be found, rather than the one seeking to find others. It is almost like we think of ourselves as a princess in a tower waiting for Prince Charming to storm the castle and set us free. Stop that. Jesus is the King and He has already freed you from your captivity through salvation. Go be a “finder.” Believe in people. Go speak life into others. You might find that it is one of the most rewarding things you ever do. In the process of finding others, you may find your life’s work.
2027-11-20.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for finding us.

2027-11-21.title: Don’t Believe the Hype
2027-11-21.verse: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck Herod down because he did not give the glory to God, and he was eaten by worms and died.
2027-11-21.observation: Herod was struck down because he believed the words of the people and did not give glory to God. When we find our identity in anything other than Christ, we will eventually fall. We cannot sustain the pressure of greatness. It is only an illusion. Our identity in Christ is not held up by our own hype or the words of other people. It is held up by the King. He can never fail and never takes a day off. He can sustain us through any darkness and valley. Put your identity in the One who can hold us up and never changes His mind.
2027-11-21.application: Find your identity in Christ and not the words of others.
2027-11-21.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for knowing us and loving us.

2027-11-22.title: The Power of Fasting
2027-11-22.verse: While they were serving the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.” Then, after they had fasted and prayed and placed their hands on them, they sent them off.
2027-11-22.observation: When it was time to know next steps, the people of God focused on humbling themselves so they could hear God’s direction more clearly. This is one of the main reasons we fast. Fasting causes us to quiet our habits, our addictions, and our appetites, so we can hear the Lord’s direction. If you have a big decision coming up, your anxiety or appetites may often be louder than the leading of the Lord. Therefore, the best thing you can do is to push away from all that. Take some time and focus on humbling yourself before the Lord with fasting. You’ll be surprised at the clarity it brings.
2027-11-22.application: What meal could you fast within the next few days? How could you replace your physical food with spiritual food? Give it a shot.
2027-11-22.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for always being willing to give direction when we humble ourselves enough to listen.

2027-11-23.title: Expect Difficulty with Joy
2027-11-23.verse: They strengthened the souls of the disciples and encouraged them to continue in the faith, saying, “We must enter the kingdom of God through many persecutions.
2027-11-23.observation: One of the odd observations by non-Christians is when they see Christians accept hardship with joy. This does not mean that they are excited about hardships or that hardships are looked for as some type of happy event. It is the lack of fear that surprises people. For Christians, it is not that we enjoy difficulty. The reality is we know that it is in the darkest moments where the light shines the brightest. Peter was able to see Jesus walk on water, but he had to be in a life-threatening storm first. Paul was visited by an angel who delivered a message of hope, but he had to be threatened with going down in a ship due to a storm. Moses received a burning bush experience, but he had to be a wanted fugitive for 40 years. God does amazing things when our back is up against the wall. That is what we call a miracle. So, we expect difficulty, but do so with joy. We know God is bigger and cannot wait to see what He does next.
2027-11-23.application: When you enter tough times, start looking for Jesus.
2027-11-23.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for walking with us through every valley.

2027-11-24.title: We All Still Have Growing To Do
2027-11-24.verse: Barnabas wanted to bring John called Mark along with them too, but Paul insisted that they should not take along this one who had left them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work. They had a sharp disagreement, so that they parted company. Barnabas took along Mark and sailed away to Cyprus,
2027-11-24.observation: This was during a time of extremes. The Holy Spirit had descended and the church was being born. The gospel was reaching people who had never heard. Paul and Barnabas had given their lives to spread the Good News everywhere. It was also a time when they were all still figuring it out. The disagreement rose because of John Mark. We do not know exactly why Paul did not want Mark to go, but it could be that Mark had left them on an earlier journey. Perhaps Paul was not ready to risk Mark leaving again. Barnabas seemed willing to take that chance. No matter, it is refreshing to see that these men were still human. They did not have it all figured out yet. They still needed grace from each other. When we don’t get things right, we can sometimes feel like there is something uniquely wrong with us. Praise the Lord for passages like this. If Paul and Barnabas were still figuring it out, it’s okay for us to still be working on things too.
2027-11-24.application: Don’t get discouraged. Just keep taking steps.
2027-11-24.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being with us through every season of growing and change.

2027-11-25.title: What Do You Bring With You?
2027-11-25.verse: As they went through the towns, they passed on the decrees that had been decided on by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the Gentile believers to obey. So the churches were being strengthened in the faith and were increasing in number every day.
2027-11-25.observation: Giving a gift when you come. I had a friend who once said that he would never go over to someone’s house for a meal or event without bringing some sort of gift. He thought it was always a blessing to be invited and it was his way of showing gratitude. After a while, it just became expected that my friend was always going to bring something to bless the house he visited. Many times it would be as simple as a plate of cookies. He just wanted to show gratitude. We all do this when we come into contact with others. We bring something with us. We bring our attitudes, our attention, our issues, our addictions, our insecurities, and the spiritual gifts the Lord has placed in our lives. The question is, what impact are they having? My friend had the impact of always being welcome and always bringing a smile to the face of those he met. How about you and me? What is the outcome of our presence? The passage says that, as they went from town to town, the churches were strengthened. What do you leave behind?
2027-11-25.application: Decide to leave a trail of blessing behind you today.
2027-11-25.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for leaving a legacy of faithfulness through our lives.

2027-11-26.title: Bring Your Brain With You
2027-11-26.verse: These Jews were more open-minded than those in Thessalonica, for they eagerly received the message, examining the scriptures carefully every day to see if these things were so. Therefore many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.
2027-11-26.observation: When I was younger, I went through a crisis of faith. I loved Jesus, but I had questions. The crisis came when I was told that I didn’t need to have questions. I just needed to have more faith. This would have probably worked for many people, but my brain is not wired that way. The result was a difficult season of thinking something was wrong because of the questions that would not go away. This passage was a gift. The people of Berea were like me. They were open-minded but not so much that their brains fell out. They wanted to study what was being presented to find the truth. Discovering this has helped me tremendously. Christianity is a “logical” belief system. Jesus says He is the Way, the Truth, and the Life. We can bring our brains into the conversation and discover the truth. The Lord is not intimidated or angered by questions. We are welcomed to bring all our doubts, questions, fears, and everything else into the discussion and find the truth that will set us free.
2027-11-26.application: Bring your questions and find the truth through logically and systematically studying the Scriptures. The truth will set you free.
2027-11-26.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for inviting us to examine our faith.

2027-11-27.title: Able to Teach, Able to Learn
2027-11-27.verse: Now a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, arrived in Ephesus. He was an eloquent speaker, well-versed in the scriptures. He had been instructed in the way of the Lord, and with great enthusiasm he spoke and taught accurately the facts about Jesus, although he knew only the baptism of John. He began to speak out fearlessly in the synagogue, but when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained the way of God to him more accurately. When Apollos wanted to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples to welcome him. When he arrived, he assisted greatly those who had believed by grace, for he refuted the Jews vigorously in public debate, demonstrating from the scriptures that the Christ was Jesus.
2027-11-27.observation: In this passage, two wonderful things happened. First, you have someone who is willing to invest their life into another. Second, you have someone willing to receive teaching in the way it is intended and grow. I have been on both sides of this equation. Both sides take a measure of humility and confidence. On the side of the teachers, you have to have the humility to be patient, pray for open doors, and then move at the speed of the person God has placed in your life. You have to also be confident because God has given you the opportunity to make a positive difference in others. On the side of the one receiving teaching, you have to have a healthy dose of humility. It can be hard to learn from others. You also have to have the confidence to understand that God is growing you so you can be more effective in the kingdom of God. The process requires a lot from both sides. However, the results are powerful for both sides.
2027-11-27.application: Find someone you love and ask them to help you get better. If you assume the posture of a student, the ability to teach will come in time.
2027-11-27.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for opening doors to grow.

2027-11-28.title: The Importance of the “Together Life”
2027-11-28.verse: Even some of the provincial authorities who were his friends sent a message to him, urging him not to venture into the theater.
2027-11-28.observation: I heard someone once say, “Make sure you have friends who are not impressed with you.” This phrase meant that we need friends who are true friends. They are not with us because of what we can do for them or for what they can do for us. We are interested in doing life together and that is enough. This means they are willing to encourage us when we win, and warn us when we are about to do something harmful. Paul had these kinds of friends. They knew it would not be wise to enter the crowd that day. Paul’s zeal for God was genuine, but the timing was off. Paul had friends who loved him enough to warn him and to see what he could not in the moment. Be the kind of friend who loves someone enough to encourage them and to warn them.
2027-11-28.application: Who do you need to warn today? Ask the Holy Spirit to open a door and be ready.
2027-11-28.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for giving us the opportunity to love others.

2027-11-29.title: Trusting God in Looming Trouble
2027-11-29.verse: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem without knowing what will happen to me there, except that the Holy Spirit warns me in town after town that imprisonment and persecutions are waiting for me. But I do not consider my life worth anything to myself, so that I may finish my task and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the good news of God’s grace.
2027-11-29.observation: In my own life, I have noticed that it is one thing to trust God when all is going well and another to trust God in the middle of a difficult storm. When things are going well, we trust God because it is easy. When things are going terribly, it is possible to trust God because we really do not have any other option. But, perhaps the most difficult time to trust God is when I see trouble coming, and it appears as though the Lord is not going to keep me from it. There are many times when we pray for God to spare us from trouble, but we have this deep feeling that the Lord is not going to take it away. An example would be when we know there is a difficult conversation coming with a friend who is walking away from the Lord. We do not want to be the one who has to confront this friend, but God has placed us in their life for a reason. Perhaps this was a little of how Jesus felt in the Garden. He asked for reprieve from the Cross, but said, “Not My will, but Your will be done.” That is a difficult prayer to pray. This is what Paul was facing. He knew that if he continued to obey God, difficulty was on the horizon. However, he decided it was better to face a storm with God, than to live in the light without Him. The same is true for us.
2027-11-29.application: Is there a storm brewing in your life? It’s okay to ask the Lord to keep you from it. However, always remember to trust the Lord no matter what. If He allows it, He will be with you through it.
2027-11-29.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for never leaving us. Not even for a moment.
